findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple instances of hand washing, which ended by using bare hands to turn off the faucet. Education was conducted as the inspector modeled proper hand washing. Ensure hand washing occurs for at least 20 seconds, with soap, and warm running water. Hand washing should conclude with drying hands with a paper towel, and then using that same paper towel to turn off the faucet (to avoid recontaminating hands).
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed the chemical sanitizing dish machine to be dispensing 0 ppm Chlorine after multiple runs. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) primed the dish machine, replaced the sanitizer bucket, and removed a broken line. Afterwards the dish machine was observed to be dispensing 50 ppm Chlorine. Ensure the dish machine is primed and tested at a frequency to ensure the proper concentration of food contact surfaces- as recommended by the manufacturer's label (50-200 ppm Chlorine).
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the facility’s test strips to have been soiled. CORRECTED- new test strips were obtained. Ensure the facility always has dry, functional test strips, to verify the concentration of the chemical sanitizing dish machine.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. [Pf]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no sanitizer bucket prepared in the kitchen during today’s inspection. CORRECTED- a new sanitizer bucket was prepared. Create a sanitizer bucket at the start of each shift to frequently sanitize food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed soil accumulation on multiple nonfood contact surfaces in the facility:
1) The gaskets of the prep cooler doors.
2) FIRST REPEAT: The shelves of the walk in cooler. 
Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of food debris, to prevent contamination of ready to eat (RTE) foods.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a personal cell phone stored on above the food preparation space in the kitchen. Discussed with the person in charge. Ensure all personal items are stored away from items for service to prevent contamination of foods.
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the hand washing sink nearest the entry of the kitchen to be out of paper towels. CORRECTED- paper towels were placed in the unit. Ensure all hand washing sinks are always stocked with warm running water, soap, and paper towels for proper hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the tamarind and tomato sauces at the front counter cooler (identified as being Temperature Control for food Safety- (TCS) by the PIC based on ingredients and processes) to be above 41F (stem thermometer reading of 56F). CORRECTED- the items were moved from the working cooler this morning, and the facility will implement TIME AS A CONTROL until the cooler is serviced. Ensure items are used or discarded within FOUR hours until the cooler is observed to be cold holding food items at 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Food items in the walk in cooler were stated to have been prepared in previous days did not have date marking. CORRECTED- the PIC placed dates on the foods and replaced old stickers that did not reflect the date of preparation. Ensure all TCS food items are date marked to be used or discarded within 7 days. The day of preparation counts as day one. Date marking must be dated based on the oldest prepared ingredient.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).[P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the under counter cooler to have an ambient temperature of 51F, and as such not properly cold holding food items (see violation #22). TCS food items must be held at or below 41F to prevent the growth of pathogens that may cause foodborne illness. Inspector will return by 03/06 to ensure the cooler has been serviced or replaced.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple prepared foods in the walk in cooler to be uncovered. Ensure all prepared foods are covered to protect from contamination in cooling units moving forward
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

findings.citation_text: 4-601.11 (A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed salmon in the walk in cooler still in its reduced oxygen packaging. Salmon packages contained a label to remove from the reduced oxygen environment upon thawing. CORRECTED- the PIC placed small cuts in the packages to take the food out of a potentially harmful environment.Ensure salmon and other packages that are in a reduced oxygen environment are opened for proper thawing to prevent the growth of Clostridium botulinum- the causative agent of Botulism
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section. [Pf]

findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT- No food handler certificate is available for the food employees during this inspection. Ensure employees complete food handler training within 30 days of hire and renew as needed. Inspector provided website to receive Food Handler certificates on the back of their business card. Keep food handler certificates available on file for review during inspections.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. [Pf]

Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. [C]
